Distribution. The female holotype comes from Taveuni Island, Fiji. The male allotype appears to come from Savusavu (also known as Savu Savu), in the south of Vanua Levu Island, Fiji. Although on separate islands, Savusavu is only 50 kilometres from Taveuni, and at their closest points the two islands are less than 10 kilometres apart. Other specimens of the type series from Fiji lack more detailed data.

Distribution. As noted above, P. cinnabarus is presently known from the vicinity of Tongren, in Guizhou Province, south-central China. Tongren is located in the northeastern part of the province, near the border with Hunan Province, at 27.731506 ° N, 109.189669 ° E. While the region is primarily at low elevations, it is also characterized by a significant amount of karst topology and steep, wooded hills, which is the most likely habitat for this species.

Distribution. Iliahia pahulu is only known from two specimens collected along the Munro Trail near the summit of Lānaihale, Lānaʻi. It is possible that this species also exists (or existed) in similar habitat on Molokaʻi and Mauna ʻEʻeka (west Maui) in the vicinity of Santalum haleakalae var. lanaiense on those islands. Conservation status. Likely critically endangered. Only ca. 30 trees of Santalum haleakalae var. lanaiense are known to still remain on Lānaʻi (USFWS 2023). Surveys on Molokaʻi and Mauna ʻEʻeka (west Maui) are badly needed to see if Iliahia pahulu occurs there in the event it or its presumed host go extinct on Lānaʻi.
